items.content:

Square Enix held the Final Fantasy XIV Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo this weekend, and during the event, they had a little bit of news about the new Evercold expansion. The big reveal for this one was that the second new job coming to the title will be called the Zephyr. What's more, they showed off what the Collector's Box will look like and some of the items it will contain. We have more details from the company here, as more will be coming in November. Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold will launch on February 23, 2027.

During the opening keynote, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed "Zephyr," the second of two new jobs arriving in Evercold . A physical ranged DPS, Zephyr joins the fray using a combination of crossbow shots and support from an avian familiar known as Nephele. Alongside the release date, Yoshida revealed that pre-orders for the Evercold expansion and the previously announced Collector's Box will start beginning Wednesday, November 4, 2026 at 10:00 a.m. PDT.

The Collector's Bundle will be available for pre-order in limited quantities exclusively from the Square Enix Store and contains the physical Collector's Box and a code for the Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold Digital Collector's Edition for Windows or Mac. PS5, PS4, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and Steam players can order the Collector's Box as a standalone product and pre-order the Evercold Digital Collector's Edition separately on their respective platforms.

The Evercold Collector's Box includes the physical goods listed below and does not include a copy of Evercold , in-game items, or pre-order bonuses.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Evercold release date delayed until February
items.summary: Producer Naoki Yoshida pushed Evercold back over quality concerns
items.content:
By Josh Broadwell Published Oct 31, 2026, 9:27 AM EDT Josh is a critic, reporter, and guide writer who covers a broad range of topics, though he specializes in narrative-driven games. He's written for some of the biggest brands in publishing, including Rolling Stone, RogerEbert.com, NPR, and Wired, and he also freelances as a video game consultant. News Producer Naoki Yoshida explains why Evercold has been pushed back

Image: Square Enix Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Sign in to your Polygon.com account Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Square Enix has delayed Final Fantasy XIV Evercold 's release date, producer Naoki Yoshida announced during the Fan Fest Tokyo event, but it's not a big delay. The MMO's expansion was originally planned for a late January launch , but Yoshida decided to delay the launch by three weeks.

Evercold 's early access launch is now set for Feb. 19, and the full launch is Feb. 23. Pre-orders begin on Nov. 4. Yoshida said the expansion's essential features were progressing smoothly, but he decided to delay for quality.

"We were on track to just barely get the game to you in the stated frame," Yoshida said. "This is being done to make sure we can deliver on the many promises we've made. We appreciate your understanding as we near the finish line."

That the team needed extra time to ensure quality isn't too surprising. Evercold will introduce a number of features new to Final Fantasy XIV , including a more open progression system for main story quests where you can pursue questlines in a less linear fashion. There's also an auto-balance adjustment system that helps ensure enemy level and duty difficulty scales to match everyone's level, in case players joining a duty are at different levels.

Evercold also changes FFXIV 's progression from daily to weekly so folks have more flexibility. If you can't play for a few days, you aren't missing out, and you can even go back and earn reward points from previous weeks if you weren't able to complete them for some reason. And Evercold adds the new Evolved battle style aimed at streamlining combat, which Yoshida said the team is still tweaking it for all the non- Evercold jobs and role actions. Square Enix is planning a whole Live Letter dedicated to how Evolved mode works sometime before Evercold 's launch.

Anyway, it's a lot to get right, and it's definitely not a set of features you'd want to launch in a buggy state.

As with previous expansions, you'll be able to start playing Evercold from the early access date only if you have an active subscription, pre-ordered Evercold , and registered the pre-order bonus code ahead of the early access launch date.

Final Fantasy XIV is available on Mac, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X.

items.title: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold Gets February 2027 Release Date
items.summary: Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold launches on February 23, 2027, with early access starting February 19 for eligible players who pre-order the expansion.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV: Evercold will launch on February 23, 2027, with early access beginning four days earlier on February 19 for eligible players who pre-order the expansion. Square Enix confirmed the release date through the MMORPG’s official account , with pre-orders scheduled to open on November 4, 2026.

Evercold is the sixth major expansion for Final Fantasy XIV and takes players to the icebound realm of the Fourth. It raises the level cap to 110 and introduces two new jobs: Bastion, a tank, and Zephyr, a physical ranged DPS job.

The expansion will also add new dungeons and cities, alongside a redesigned job action system. Players will be able to choose between two combat modes, Evolved and Reborn. The former offers a streamlined approach, while the latter retains the traditional combat system.

Final Fantasy XIV originally launched in 2010 but received a negative reception, prompting Square Enix to rebuild the MMORPG before relaunching it in 2013 as A Realm Reborn. The game has since received five major expansions: Heavensward, Stormblood, Shadowbringers, Endwalker, and Dawntrail.

items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV Online (Switch 2) - An Expansive Port That Demands Your Commitment
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Online has been through quite a rollercoaster journey over the years on its way to becoming one of the most respected MMOs in the industry. Its 2010 launch was a disaster, plagued with performance issues and shoddy design that torpedoed its reputation.

Rather than pulling the plug early, Square decided to swap in a new director to salvage it, leading to a reboot in 2013 called A Realm Reborn. Since then, the game has mostly gone from strength to strength across over a decade of expansions and is now in the process of building up its second major arc.

Though this isn’t the first time Square Enix has brought Final Fantasy XIV to console, it is the first time it’s come to a Nintendo platform, and I’m happy to report that it stuck the landing. The full fat experience is here in all its glory, giving you access to a high quality and addictive RPG experience that’s sure to be in the running for one of the most content-rich games ever produced for a handheld.

The narrative places you in the role of a self-insert character in the land of Eorzea who comes into the picture just as geopolitical tensions are on the rise. After a catastrophic war five years earlier, the expansionist Garlean Empire was repelled by the city-states comprising the Eorzean Alliance, but its leaders desire revenge and are winding up for another grab at ultimate control.

Amid this, you’re also told through a vision by a mysterious goddess of light named Hydaelyn that you’re her chosen champion, and she tasks you with finding six magical crystals to ward off the servants of an approaching darkness.

Thus, we set off on the early steps of what came to be called the Hydaelyn-Zodiark Saga, a four-part fantasy epic that should take you no less than two-hundred hours to complete, and that’s assuming that you beeline for the finale and engage in almost no side content. After all that, there’s then a whole other expansion that’s in the early stages of setting up the next ten-year arc.

Suffice to say, Final Fantasy XIV features one of the richest storylines available in a modern RPG, weaving together the subplots of various nations, factions, and supporting characters to make for an impressively complex and deep narrative.

The downside to this, however, is that the pacing can be all over the place. The 60-hour story of the base game alone is basically an extended exposition dump detailing all the major players in the world and setting the stage for the building conflict to come, meaning you spend a lot of time scrolling through line after line of unvoiced text from NPCs telling you about very interesting story beats that happened some other time offscreen.

This leads to a narrative experience with some incredible highs and disappointing lows. Once the plot picks up steam and starts focusing more on current events, there are lots of awesome character moments and payoffs that make all the time investment up to that point feel worth it. Yet between those moments, it can sometimes feel like the plot really takes its time focusing on largely irrelevant or uninteresting subjects that you simply have to endure to reach the good stuff.

Gameplay design follows the expected structure of an MMO, giving you an enormous living world to explore packed with jobs and levels to grind, side quests to fulfill, minigames to fool around with, dungeons to raid, and a massive story to gradually uncover.

As long as you stick to the Main Story Quest chain, you'll be toured around all the main points of interest in an area and progressively introduced to core mechanics and objectives at a measured pace. Side quest content then fills out the world with more detail and texture, though tons of the quest objectives admittedly boil down to 'bring me three boar skins' fetch quests.

A big part of what makes the gameplay loop so addicting is the versatility of your character, who can independently level dozens of jobs that fill out various combat and non-combat roles. In a combat role, your job is built around a growing variety of cooldown-based actions, echoing the classic Final Fantasy ATB system that blends turn-based and action gameplay.

Every combat job has its own distinct gimmicks and features, such as how the Thaumaturge operates by repeatedly shifting between two passive states that bolster either damage output or MP regeneration. Mechanics like this keep fights from feeling too much like you’re just watching cooldown icons on a hotbar, and there are enough distinguishing traits to make the various classes all feel like they’re worth experimenting with.

Non-combat roles are just as dynamic, even without the pressure of attacking foes. If you're working as a Goldsmith, you can create various bits of armour and jewellery, and it's much more involved than merely clicking the 'Craft' button on a menu after you have the materials.

PlayStation®5, PlayStation®4, XBOX Series X|S, Nintendo Switch™ 2 and Steam players can order the Collector’s Box as a standalone product and pre-order the Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition separately on their respective platforms. items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Delayed Till February 2027
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Delayed, New Release Date Announced at FFXIV Fan Fest
items.summary: The MMORPG's next expansion was set to launch shortly after the new year, but Warriors of Light will have to wait a bit longer.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold was set to launch sometime in January 2027, which was announced as part of its initial reveal back in April this year during the North American FFXIV Fan Fest. However, this next expansion for the critically acclaimed MMORPG has been delayed – FFXIV Evercold's release date is now February 23, 2027 (and February 19, 2027 for early access). This was announced alongside the new, full trailer / intro cinematic for Evercold at FFXIV Fan Fest in Japan, and was said to only be a four-week delay.

In typical FFXIV fashion, the third and final teaser trailer is the full opening cinematic for an expansion, and it kicked off the Japan Fan Fest keynote where director and producer Naoki Yoshida presented more details on new features, where the ongoing story is headed, and fundemental gameplay changes as FFXIV goes into version 8.0 alongside Evercold's launch.

Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 and will come with several bonus items, which will be revealed later in the Fan Fest keynote - I will update this as they are shown. Additionally, we got a glimpse of the second new Job coming to his new expansion. It's a ranged DPS called Zephyr, which rocks a crossbow as their primary weapon and commands an avian companion to provide support.

There's a lot coming to FFXIV Evercold in addition to a new world and main story including a Neon Genesis Evangelion crossover raid series , a Final Fantasy VII crossover raid series, a new Tank Job with Bastion, and much more. Be sure to check out my Dawntrail review as well to look back at the last expansion before heading into this new era for FFXIV.

items.title: How to get Tifa and Barret's outfits in FFXIV
items.content:
By Paulo Kawanishi Published Oct 28, 2026, 1:50 PM EDT Guides How fast can you type "Nibelheim"?

Image: Square Enix via Polygon Add Polygon.com on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover Summary Generate a summary of this story Jump links Jump Links How to get Tifa and Barret's outfits in FFXIV How to start the Keybound Brawler event in FFXIV All FFXIV Keybound Brawler rewards Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Tifa and Barret's outfits are the real stars in Final Fantasy 14 ' s event in the Keybound Brawlers , a new collaboration with Final Fantasy 7 . Unlike Cloud's outfit, which is based on the Final Fantasy 7: Advent Children design and has been in the game for ages, these two are based on the FF7 remake project. To get them and many other FF7 -themed cosmetics and items, you must survive the typing brawls and earn a special currency.

Below, you can find all the information you need to learn how to get Tifa and Barret's outfits in FFXIV .

You can only obtain Tifa and Barret's outfit by participating in the Keybound Brawler event , which runs from Oct. 28, until the release of Final Fantasy 14 's patch 8.0 with the Evercold expansion (which should be in January).

The only prerequisites for participating in the event are reaching level 15 , completing one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy", and unlocking the Gold Saucer . As one might expect given the name, you also need a keyboard to play this game.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon By winning matches during the event, you earn the Manderville Gold Saucer Credits (MGC), which you can exchange for the outfits at the MGC Trader in the Keybound Square. This currency is different from the Manderville Gold Saucer Points (MGP), which you obtain by participating in the regular Gold Saucer's activities.

To purchase all four pieces of Tifa's outfit , you will need 1,380 MGC , and for Barret's five pieces , you'll need 1,570 MGC (I'm not considering both the Avalanche Brawler's Earring and the Avalanche Leader's Earring in these sums). If you complete all three waves of a brawl, you can earn from 200-340 MGC depending on your final score . This means that you will need six to 12 matches to earn enough credits to purchase all the pieces of both outfits.

Keep in mind that the outfits are gender locked when deciding which ones to prioritize.

Graphic: Paulo Kawanishi/Polygon | Source images: Square Enix via Polygon While the Keybound Brawler event is taking place, you can start it by traveling to the Gold Saucer in Thanalan and talking to the Catlike Mammet (5.4, 7.0) to accept the "Keyward Bound" side quest .

Next, you will need to talk to W'zazanh at the Wonder Square (6.1, 7.3) to enter the Keybound Square. Once inside, interact with the Magitype Master behind the counter to complete the quest. Since there are no crystals to teleport to the area, you will always need to talk to W'zazanh to return the Keybound Square in the future.

Graphic: Paulo Kawanishi/Polygon | Source images: Square Enix via Polygon To play Keybound Brawler matches, you need to talk to the Keybound Registrar NPC (5.8, 6.0) . While it's possible to queue as a group, you can also go solo and wait for the game to find party members for you.

Each match is divided into three waves, during which enemies will try to approach the barrier in front of your party. If they reach it, enemies will attack the barrier, lowering your party's HP bar. To attack them, you must correctly type the words that appear above them. Pay attention because, although you don't need to distinguish between uppercase and lowercase, both punctuation and accents count . If enemies deplete your party's HP bar, you will fail the brawl.

Image: Square Enix via Polygon By simply participating in a match, you will earn some MGC, but your score and the number of waves you survive affect the final amount. If you complete the last wave, in addition to MGC and MGP, you also earn a keybound coffer . These can contain various rewards, from food to weapons like the Adamant Rod.

The Keybound Brawler event offers all kinds of rewards, ranging from the two Tifa and Barret's outfits to the unique mount Magitek Scorpion. You can only obtain these rewards by exchanging MGC except for the aforementioned coffers, which you also earn whenever you defeat the third wave's boss.

items.title: Keybound Brawler Arrives October 28!
items.summary: Keybound Brawler, a new event that tests your typing prowess, is coming to the Manderville Gold Saucer! The first iteration of the event will be a special collaboration with the FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE series. Participate in the collaborat
items.content:
Keybound Brawler, a new event that tests your typing prowess, is coming to the Manderville Gold Saucer! The first iteration of the event will be a special collaboration with the FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE series. Participate in the collaboration stages to obtain MGC which can be exchanged for numerous rewards, including collaboration attire, a mount, emote, and more!

Event Duration

From Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 19:00 (AEDT) to the release of Patch 8.0 * The end date listed on Steam does not reflect the release date for Patch 8.0.

How to Participate

Begin the quest "Keyward Bound" by speaking to the Catlike Mammet in The Gold Saucer (X:5.4 Y:7.0). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy." * Players must first complete the quest "It Could Happen to You" to be able to travel to the Manderville Gold Saucer via airship from any of the three city-states. * Please note that a keyboard is required to participate in this content. Gamepads and on-screen keyboards cannot be used.

Rewards

* After this collaboration event has ended, it will be held as a special event at irregular intervals. Visit the special site for more details.

From Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 9:00 (BST) / 19:00 (AEDT) to Tuesday, October 27, 2026 at 7:59 a.m. (PDT) / 14:59 (GMT) / Wednesday, 28 October at 1:59 (AEDT)

How to Participate

Begin the quest "It Could Happen to You" by speaking to the Well-heeled Youth in Ul'dah – Steps of Nald (X:9.6 Y:9.0). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy." * Players can travel to the Manderville Gold Saucer via airship from any of the three city-states upon completing this quest.

Rewards

* This event is identical to the one previously held. * Players who have already completed the quest during a previous event release may immediately resume playing the collaboration content. * After this collaboration event has ended, it will be held as a special event at irregular intervals. Visit the special site for more details.

items.content: Faced with the coming Solstice, the fate Halmarut claims to await all worlds, the Warrior of Light embarks upon another journey─one that promises to grow ever colder... Patch 7.56 also introduces the new limited job beastmaster and its exclusive duty, the Crucible of the Unbroken. Furthermore, weekly restrictions have been removed and the Echo enabled in AAC Heavyweight Tier (Savage). Read the full patch notes on the Lodestone.
